metadata.case_name: CHENG WAI CHUN v. CHAN KWAN YIU & ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: worked in the family business operated by her husband which was a canteen in Tsuen Wan; worked as cashier and waitress

injuries.description: collapse fracture (wedging) of the T12 vertebra
source: subsequent X-ray confirmed a collapse fracture of the T12 vertebra.
Both doctors agree that the X-ray films show wedging of the T12 vertebra.

injuries.description: open bimalleolar fracture of the right ankle; comminuted fracture of the distal right fibia and tibula with 3 cm x 3 cm laceration over the lateral side of the right ankle with bone sticking out
source: she was found to have a 3 cm x 3 cm wide laceration over the lateral side of the right ankle with bone sticking out.
X-rays showed a comminuted fracture of the distal right fibia and tibula.
she ... had an emergency operation for open reduction and internal fixation of the open bimalleolar fracture of the right ankle.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple injuries of ankle or foot

injuries.description: permanent scarring on the right ankle and a scar on the inner right thigh from which skin was taken for grafting
injuries.body_part: right ankle and inner right thigh
source: she has a nasty scar on the right ankle and another one at the site on her inner thigh, from which the skin was taken for grafting.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: persistent pain in the lower back
local tenderness was found over the left loin
weakness and numbness of the left leg
pain in her ankle which comes on if she has to stand or walk for an hour
severe initial right ankle pain after the accident
anxiety, depression and concern over the well-being of the fetus
10% permanent impairment of the whole person in respect of the back injury
2% permanent impairment in respect of the ankle injury

treatments_received: emergency operation for open reduction and internal fixation of the open bimalleolar fracture of the right ankle
ankle wound treated with a skin graft taken from the inner right thigh on 19 April 2000
referred for pressure therapy for the scar
implants were taken out in March 2001
reasonable period of sick leave would have been 18 months
treatments_future: intradermal steroid injections for the thigh scar

losses.description: Persistent lower back pain and 10% permanent impairment of the whole person in respect of the back injury (collapse fracture of T12); persistent effects of right ankle injury with 2% permanent impairment

Nasty scar on the right ankle and scar on the inner thigh causing embarrassment and restriction in choice of dress; cosmetic deformity assessed (disputed assessments: 10% by Dr Hsieh, 4% by Dr Nicholson)
